algorithm.Title: Weakness (Generalized) and Fatigue - Female (Child)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Child | Female
Definition: Generalized weakness/fatigue assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published when-to-get-help guidance.

KeyPoints: Persistent unexplained fatigue can be associated with sleep problems, mood disorders, anaemia, diabetes, thyroid disease, infection, or other medical conditions.
Sudden focal weakness, chest pain, severe breathing difficulty, confusion, or reduced responsiveness is an emergency presentation.
Fatigue lasting weeks or interfering with normal life warrants clinical assessment.
Background.ExpertReviewer: PENDING: Qatar adult, pediatric, obstetric, emergency, specialty, mental-health, and nursing governance review

FirstAid: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for sudden or one-sided weakness, inability to stand, confusion, fainting, seizure, abnormal breathing, chest pain, major bleeding, severe infection, pregnancy/postpartum danger signs, suspected poisoning, or an unwell/floppy child. Keep the person still and do not give food, drink, or medicine if consciousness or swallowing is impaired. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Is a measured blood-glucose reading below 4 mmol/L, or are symptoms suggesting hypoglycaemia, in a person with diabetes?
questions.Information: A confirmed low reading or hypoglycaemia symptom pattern belongs in the authored Diabetes - Low Blood Sugar pathway.

questions.Question: Is a measured blood-glucose reading high, with thirst, frequent urination, vomiting, abdominal pain, drowsiness, or other hyperglycaemia symptoms?
questions.Information: A confirmed high reading or hyperglycaemia symptom pattern belongs in the authored Diabetes - High Blood Sugar pathway.

questions.Question: Is there sudden one-sided weakness or numbness, slurred speech, chest pain, severe difficulty breathing, or is the person confused or difficult to rouse?
questions.Information: Universal emergency rule-out added ahead of the tiredness/fatigue guidance itself - sudden focal weakness or altered consciousness may indicate stroke or another acute emergency rather than simple fatigue.

questions.Question: Has the tiredness lasted a few weeks without a clear cause, is it affecting daily life, or is it accompanied by weight loss, mood changes, or gasping/snorting/choking sounds during sleep?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends a GP visit for unexplained, persistent, or functionally-impairing tiredness, or tiredness with these associated symptoms.

questions.Question: Is this a normal, occasional tiredness with a clear cause and none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance: it's normal to feel tired sometimes; sleep hygiene and lifestyle measures are appropriate first steps.

advice.Title: Qatar emergency generalized-weakness response
Content: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for sudden or one-sided weakness, inability to stand, confusion, fainting, seizure, abnormal breathing, chest pain, major bleeding, severe infection, pregnancy/postpartum danger signs, suspected poisoning, or an unwell/floppy child. Keep the person still and do not give food, drink, or medicine if consciousness or swallowing is impaired. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: worsening or one-sided weakness; loss of consciousness, seizure, or confusion; abnormal breathing, chest pain, bleeding, or severe infection.

advice.Title: Routine fatigue follow-up
Content: Book a routine GP appointment to investigate persistent or unexplained tiredness.
Call Back If: new symptoms develop; worsening weight loss.

advice.Title: Home care for occasional tiredness
Content: Maintain a balanced diet and regular activity, keep consistent sleep times aiming for 6-9 hours, relax before bed, and avoid smoking, excess alcohol, caffeine, and screens close to bedtime.
Call Back If: tiredness persists for weeks; new symptoms develop.

references: NHS.UK, "Tiredness and fatigue", https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/tiredness-and-fatigue/ (page last reviewed 02 June 2023)

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: What is the person's exact age and sex, are they pregnant/recently postpartum, and did weakness start suddenly or gradually? Clarify generalized versus one-sided/focal weakness and child feeding, behaviour, urine, and safeguarding concerns.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: Any unintentional weight loss, mood changes, or other new symptoms?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant source assessment retained from the Batch 3 runtime protocol.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: Is this affecting daily activities?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant source assessment retained from the Batch 3 runtime protocol.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: What change has the parent or caregiver observed in behaviour, alertness, eating or drinking, sleep, school or play, and normal activity?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Child assessment includes caregiver-observed functional change and cannot rely only on adult-style self-report.
